title: Media failure never blocks learning
statement: Give every media element a working fallback, so a clip, image or video that fails leaves readable text or the screens it duplicates instead of blocking the learner.
detail: The golden student-course standard accepts a media element only with, among other things, a load test and a failure fallback, and lists media failure that blocks learning as a failure signal. A Grade 5 course's review profile rejects a failed clip that leaves no readable or manual route, and its student flow shows read-to-me as active only once audio really plays, with retry and a visible self-read fallback on failure. A Grade 3 player run without audio renders every line as text and blocks nothing, and that build's background video removes itself on a load error, leaving the screens it duplicates.
against: Builds disagree on what the fallback may be: a Grade 5 release gate lets the browser read the exact authored text aloud after the learner's consent when server audio can't play (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/G5_STUDENT_EXPERIENCE_RELEASE_GATE.qmd`, line 52), while a record already there allows only the text in silence, never a synthetic voice.

evidence.quote: Each asset has a purpose, factual and rights review, equivalent-access treatment, stable layout, load test, and failure fallback.
Autoplay chains teaching moves, controls disappear, or a failed clip leaves no readable/manual route.
read-to-me appears active only after audio really plays, and failure exposes retry plus a visible self-read fallback;
If neither path starts, the failure must remain visible, offer retry, and leave self-reading available.
Run locally without audio: the player degrades gracefully — every line renders as text and
On `error` the frame and skip button REMOVE themselves, so a missing mp4 degrades to the level-set screens rather than to a broken box.
